ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: the figure shows a structure in which a benzene ring on the left is fused with a nitrogen-containing six-membered ring on the right; at the bottom of the right ring is an N-H marked with a positive charge, the upper-right carbon is connected to OH and R2, and the lower-right ring carbon is connected to R1. The curved arrows in the figure indicate redistribution of electrons within the ring toward the nitrogen-containing ring. Reasoning: after pushing according to the arrows, a new double bond forms between the ring carbon bearing R1 and the carbon bearing OH/R2; N-H changes from a positive center to neutral N-H and remains in the six-membered ring as a single bond; the fused benzene ring on the left maintains aromaticity. After using [*] to represent R1 and R2, the product can be encoded as OC1([*])c2c(NC([*])=C1)cccc2.

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure: a benzene ring fused to a nitrogen-containing six-membered ring, with N-H positively charged, an OH-bearing carbon also bonded to R2 at the top right, and R1 on the lower-right ring carbon. Apply the depicted arrows to shift the ring electrons: form the new double bond between the R1-bearing carbon and the OH/R2-bearing carbon, convert the N center to neutral N-H single-bonded within the ring, and preserve the fused aromatic benzene. Then encode the resulting graph as a SMILES with OH on C1 bearing [*], fused benzene c2...cccc2, neutral NC([*]) connected into the ring, giving OC1([*])c2c(NC([*])=C1)cccc2.
